analysis: Examined base_text units of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json lines 6862-9139. These lines lie outside the changed base ranges (changes at 3024-4003, 4824, 43813-54138). They contain unchanged golden vectors: tool_call_arguments_bridge, tool_function_extra_keys and tools, with request/provider bodies, template_input, plan hashes and token_ids. In tool_function_extra_keys (8216-8288), extra keys strict/response/examples are dropped from template_input. In tools (8677-8713), forced tool_choice injects system/user instructions and additional_context enable_thinking=false. The patch excerpt elsewhere adds additional_context enable_thinking=false at head 3020-3022 and recomputes prompt_token_count/chain_hash; this is consistent with the existing tool_choice handling seen at base 8710-8712. These are test fixtures for prompt rendering and prefix-cache block chain hashes. They are relevant to T-041 (prefix-cache hashing) only as expected values and introduce no runtime control, key, attestation (TB-011) or transport (TB-002) change. No security regression is identifiable from fixture data. Integration should confirm that the Swift/coordinator template code changes accompanying these fixture updates keep chain_hash scoping (scope_id) per-tenant and that the enable_thinking injection is coordinator-derived, not consumer-forgeable in a way that alters cache keys across tenants.
